I’m not able to actually contact HVAC companies or set up an appointment on your behalf in this environment, so I can’t complete the booking itself.

I can, however, help you do it smoothly. Here’s a simple approach you can follow:

1. Search for local HVAC companies  
   - Use terms like “HVAC annual maintenance near me” in Google/Maps/Yelp/Angi.  
   - Filter for: rating 4.5+ (if available), at least 50 reviews, and “licensed & insured” in the description.

2. Check what they include in “annual maintenance”  
   Prioritize companies that list:  
   - Full inspection of furnace/air handler and outdoor unit  
   - Coil cleaning, condensate drain check, blower cleaning  
   - Refrigerant level check, electrical and safety checks  
   - Filter check/replacement

3. Call 2–3 top candidates  
   Ask each one:  
   - “What’s included in your annual maintenance tune-up?”  
   - “Is the technician licensed and insured?”  
   - “What’s the total price, including any service fees?”  
   - “Do you offer any warranty on the work?”  
   - “When is your next available appointment for a maintenance visit?”

4. When booking the appointment  
   Have ready:  
   - Your full address and best contact phone/email  
   - Type of system (e.g., central AC + gas furnace, heat pump, mini-split) and age if you know it  
   - Preferred days/times (e.g., weekday mornings)  
   - Any current minor issues (odd noises, rooms not cooling evenly, etc.)

If you’d like, tell me:
- Your city/ZIP
- What type of HVAC system you have (or what you know about it)
- Your preferred days/times

I’ll tailor a short call script and checklist you can use when you call or request quotes online.</action>

<action type="say">
Here’s a compact set of questions you can have ready for the technician on the day of your annual maintenance:

System condition and lifespan
- “Overall, how is the system’s condition?”
- “Based on what you see, how many more years would you expect this system to last?”
- “Are there any parts that are likely to fail in the next 1–2 years?”

Efficiency and comfort
- “Is the system running as efficiently as it should for its age?”
- “Are there any adjustments or small upgrades that would noticeably improve efficiency or comfort?”
- “Do you see anything in the ductwork or airflow that might affect room-to-room comfort?”

Maintenance and filters
- “What type and size of air filter do you recommend for this system?”
- “How often should I change the filter in my specific case (given my home and usage)?”
- “Is there any basic maintenance I should be doing myself between annual visits?”

Safety and reliability
- “Did you see any safety concerns (electrical, gas, condensate drainage, refrigerant leaks, etc.)?”
- “Is there anything you recommend fixing now to avoid a breakdown during peak season?”

Repairs vs. replacement
- “If a major component fails, what cost range would repairs be versus replacement?”
- “At what point would you say it’s no longer worth repairing this system?”

Before they leave
- “What exactly did you do today as part of the maintenance?”
- “Are there any notes or photos you can share for my records?”
- “When would you recommend scheduling the next maintenance visit?”

You can print this or keep it on your phone and just check off what you’ve asked as you go.</action>
